choices.content: Two congruent figures must be reflections of each other across a line.
Two figures that are reflections of each other must have a common point.
If folding a figure along a line makes its two sides coincide, these two figures are said to be reflections of each other.
Two figures that are reflections of each other must be congruent.

question.prompt: Which statement about two figures being reflections of each other across a line is correct?

solutions.explanation:
Two figures that are reflections of each other coincide completely when folded along the axis of reflection, so they must be congruent. Thus D is true. Congruent figures are not necessarily related by a single reflection, and a reflected pair can lie entirely on opposite sides of the axis with no common point.

In C, if 'these two figures' refers to the two coinciding halves, the fold line reflects one half onto the other, so C is also true. If it refers to two whole figures, only one whole figure has been introduced. Consequently, the displayed wording does not justify D as the unique correct choice.
solutions.title: Folding and the meaning of choice C
